sketch: Smallest instance (assumption): n=3 qubits, m=1 or 2 (2^m-term states). Registers: control qubits c (Hadamard-prepared) and target qubits t, all in computational basis input |x> for x in {0..7}. Step 1: for each of the 2^n computational basis inputs |x>, apply Hadamard on m chosen qubits (standard Bell-like fan-out: H gives (|0>+(-1)^{x_i}|1>)/sqrt2). Step 2: apply a multi-qubit controlled-unitary (e.g. CNOT-type multi-target X fan-out, or controlled-Z/phase-type gate) from the m Hadamard qubits to the remaining n-m qubits, with the controlled operation chosen as a distinct computational-basis permutation per control string (e.g. target gets X^{f(c)}, f an injective linear map over GF(2)). Output states are of form 2^{-m/2} sum_{c in {0,1}^m} (-1)^{x_c·c} |c>|f(c) xor y>, which are 2^m-term superpositions with amplitudes ±1/sqrt(2^m). Orthonormality: the map x -> output is the unitary U = CU (H^{⊗m}⊗I) applied to orthonormal basis, so the 2^n outputs form an orthonormal basis; sign patterns (from input bits on Hadamard qubits) and offsets y (input bits on target qubits) label states uniquely, and unitarity forces equal-magnitude amplitudes in this family. Circuit: build_circuit(instance) compiles H on m qubits then CNOT fan-out/multi-controlled gates with explicit parameters, given a chosen input basis index x loaded by X gates; the unitary is measurement-free. Decoding: apply inverse circuit and read the computational basis to recover x, verifying basis orthonormality by checking the Gram matrix of the 2^n output columns. Different controlled-unitary choices (X-type vs. phase/Z-type or different f) yield different bases whose entanglement (concurrence/negativity/monogamy score) could be compared offline; this is not implemented in the circuit. Qudit extension (Fourier gate and generalized shift-controlled gates) and the entanglement/monogamy analysis are outside scope.
